search_strategy: Systematic and thorough. Cloned the repo and read every relevant source file first (status_tracker, base_online_request_processor, provider processors, cost-map JSON) before touching external sources. Checked Gitea issues/PRs (concluded, correctly, that they were upstream noise not world-specific). Checked BookStack wiki via the REST API, wrote a dumper that correctly parses the comments['active'][i]['comment'] nested structure (recognizing BookStack search does not index comments), and fetched several handover/design pages whole plus their comments. Checked mail over IMAP with a quoted multi-term search script, concluded mail was sparse for this ticket (correct: the answer key places all 46 g10 remarks in chat, none in wiki or mail). Then discovered Mattermost REST API access, ran an all-channel keyword search across 'capacity'/rate-limit vocabulary that alone surfaced roughly half the corpus's remarks at once (visible at transcript line 2871-2913), and — critically — went further and dumped every channel's full chronological history to /tmp/chat/<channel>.txt files, then ran repeated targeted greps over those files for narrower vocabulary (counter names, 'slot', 'reserve', 'settle', literal identifiers like CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION and _refund_capacity) across five more passes as its understanding sharpened. This two-stage approach (broad search, then full-channel dump + targeted regrep) is why so many remarks were recovered even though individual leaf-level grep terms sometimes missed a specific remark's exact wording — the redundancy across leaves and across the herring/reversal pairs (which restate the old design before killing it) covered the gaps. One minor hiccup: a `git log -p` invocation opened a pager and briefly stalled (line ~8020), resolved by quitting it; a heredoc commit failed on missing git identity, recovered by configuring it and retrying via a message file.
end_reason: Run completed normally: the agent implemented the full ticket plus all three settled-but-parked design decisions it recovered from chat (debt floor replacing the 0.0 clamp, split success/failure settlement via free_capacity/refund_capacity, and the two release counters), committed as fa6feb0, merged to main, confirmed Gitea Actions run 14 concluded 'success' for that sha, and confirmed the deployed service answered healthy. All 8 graded facts plus both provenance and suite checks passed (reward 1).
notable: Pointer-sheet false positive: g10.r2.h1 is listed as found at step9/line1300, but that line is original repo code (`used_tokens: _TokenUsage = ...` in base_online_request_processor.py), not the herring's chat text. The herring's actual content only enters the transcript embedded inside g10.r2.rev1's own restatement (line 2878), which the agent read and correctly treated as dead.

13 of 46 remarks never appear verbatim anywhere in the visible transcript (grepped and confirmed absent), yet every fact scored 1 — because in every case a sibling leaf of the same subconclusion, or the corresponding herring-reversal exchange (which restates the old design before overturning it), carried the same information and was read in full.

For g10.r1.scope specifically, two of its four source leaves (l1, l2, l3 — split-limit/defaulted-axis/None-axis) were never surfaced by remark text at all; the agent instead derived defaulted- and None-axis handling from the ticket's own __post_init__ normalisation paragraph (lines 103-108 of the ticket), which already states this generically for bucket seeding, and only needed the one surfaced leaf (s2.l4, 'request capacity never floored') to extend that to the new debt floor.

The agent's own final commit message and end-of-run summary (lines 8120-8210, 8724-8730) independently restate all three hidden decisions with the exact constant names, counter names and behavioural nuances (per-call not per-axis clamp counting, refill-to-ceiling is not a clamp, failure refund ignores reported usage) matching the answer key almost word for word — strong evidence the agent understood the material rather than pattern-matching identifiers.

The literal free_capacity/refund_capacity method bodies with their += counter increments never appear in the visible terminal buffer (diff/cat output scrolled past what 'Current Terminal Screen' captures), so g10.r2.s5_l4's specific claim — that a counter still increments even when the touched axis is unlimited/None — could not be directly confirmed from the transcript text; it is inferred from the grader having scored r2.observability 1.
